nahhas-irab:1-3.t: إِذَا السَّماءُ انْفَطَرَتْ (1): [the verb is feminine] because السماء is feminine in the most eloquent usage; al-Farrāʾ reported the masculine for it. Whoever makes it feminine forms its diminutive as سميّة, even though it is of four letters in origin, because a letter has been dropped from it. السماء is nominative by an implied verb, and likewise وَإِذَا الْكَواكِبُ انْتَثَرَتْ (2), and likewise وَإِذَا الْبِحارُ فُجِّرَتْ (3). It is not permissible that it be nominative by the other [overt] verb, except according to something ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān reported to us from Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā Thaʿlab, who said: [in] زيد قام, [Zayd] is nominative by its verb, which is intended to be placed after it. It was said: the meaning of وَإِذَا الْبِحارُ فُجِّرَتْ (3) is that some of them were made to burst into others, because of the convulsion of the earth with the passing away of the mountains and the earthquakes, so that some seas mingled with others.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: [وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ, in the second person. Translator's note: this entry continues the sentence of the previous one.] Abū Jaʿfar said: I do not know what he reported from some of the people of Medina, and I know of no one besides him who related it.

nahhas-irab:11-12.t: كِراماً كاتِبِينَ (11) is a naʿt (adjective) of حافظين, and likewise يَعْلَمُونَ ما تَفْعَلُونَ (12).

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: إِنَّ الْأَبْرارَ لَفِي نَعِيمٍ (13): i.e. those who were righteous through obedience to Allah and avoidance of His acts of disobedience. Al-Ḥasan said: الأبرار are those who do not harm [even] the tiny ants.

nahhas-irab:14-15.t: [يَصْلَوْنَها is feminine] on the basis that النار is feminine, even though الجحيم is masculine.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: Al-Farrāʾ said: That is, once they have been made to enter it, they will not come out of it. Qatāda said: [يوم الدين is] the day people are requited for their deeds.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: It was said: this is not a repetition. The meaning is: "And what will make you know what is in the Day of Judgement of punishment and exemplary chastisement for the wicked? Then what will make you know what is in the Day of Judgement of bliss for the righteous?"

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: يَوْمَ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئاً is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī. Al-Farrāʾ said «in his book on the meanings» [Maʿānī al-Qurʾān]: the readers agreed on the accusative of «يوم لا تملك». Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a mistake. Abū ʿAmr, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Isḥāq and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj — who is one of the two teachers of Nāfiʿ — read يَوْمُ لا تَمْلِكُ in the nominative. [Translator's note: the source prints the vowel of the cited reading as fatḥa.] For whoever reads the nominative, the implied form is "it is يَوْمُ لا تَمْلِكُ"; it may also be a badal (substitute) for what precedes it: ثُمَّ ما أَدْراكَ ما يَوْمُ الدِّينِ (18) يَوْمَ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئاً. For whoever reads the accusative, the implied form is "the judgement is on the day when [a soul] does not possess", and like it is وَما أَدْراكَ مَا الْقارِعَةُ يَوْمَ يَكُونُ النَّاسُ [al-Qāriʿa: 3, 4], i.e. the Calamity is on the day when people will be. It is also possible that the implied form is "they will burn in it on the Day of Judgement, يَوْمَ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئاً". These are two views, the first being the preferable of them. Al-Farrāʾ has a third view: he permitted «يوم» to be in the position of the nominative, but made indeclinable (mabnī), as the poet said: [al-ṭawīl] 546- على حين عاتبت المشيب على الصّبا (At the time when I reproached grey hair for [the loss of] youth). Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a mistake. According to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, adverbs cannot be made indeclinable together with something declinable, and the imperfect verb is declinable. As for al-Kisāʾī, he permitted that in poetry out of necessity, and the Book of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, is not to be interpreted on the basis of something like this. Rather, adverbs of time are made indeclinable together with the past verb, as in the verse, because adverbs of time are transient, not fixed, so you may make them indeclinable together with what follows them when that is not declinable, or decline them according to their original state, as in the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He: وَمِنْ خِزْيِ يَوْمِئِذٍ [Hūd: 66], declining يوم, or, if you wish, وَمِنْ خِزْيِ يَوْمَئِذٍ. [Translator's note: the source prints both variants as «يَوْمِئِذٍ»; the second, with the indeclinable fatḥa, is supplied from the sense.] On this basis يوم is made indeclinable with «إذ» on the fatḥa in the positions of nominative, genitive and accusative; and likewise وَالْأَمْرُ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلَّهِ.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: He is saying: they were overturned (بحثرت). Al-Farrāʾ interpreted it as the earth being overturned so that it cast out the treasures and the dead in it, and he cited as evidence the ḥadīth «تلقي الأرض أفلاذ كبدها» ("The earth will cast out the pieces of its liver"). Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a mistake. The Qur'an does not have "and when the earth"; in it is specifically the graves. And «وتلقي أفلاذ كبدها» — there is no disagreement among the people of knowledge that it is at the end of time and not on the Day of Resurrection. [Translator's note: the source has «أفلا كبدها» in its second citation of the ḥadīth, a misprint for «أفلاذ».]

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
[عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ ما قَدَّمَتْ وَأَخَّرَتْ] completes the statement, and it is the answer (jawāb) of «إذا». There are two views on its meaning. Ibn Zayd said: ما قدمت is what it did, and ما أخّرت is what it left, neglected and deferred of what it was commanded to put forward of the command of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He. The other view is that the meaning of ما أخّرت is a practice (sunna) that it established and that was acted upon after it. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is from Ibn ʿAbbās, and it is preferable; the people of ḥadīth hold it, while some of the people of whims (ahl al-ahwāʾ) reject it.
The evidence of its soundness is that when a person neglects what he was commanded and defers it, that is among the evil he has put forward, not among what he has deferred.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: ما is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and it is a complete noun; the kāf is in the position of the accusative by غرّ.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: [فَعَدَّلَكَ with doubling] is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries, the people of Basra and the people of Syria. The Kufans read فَعَدَلَكَ without doubling. Al-Farrāʾ considered it unlikely, even though it is the reading of his own school, because one only says عدلته إلى كذا ("I turned him to such-and-such") and صرفته إليه, and one hardly says عدّلته في كذا or صرّفته. Abū Jaʿfar said about it: This is a mistake, because the statement is complete at «فعدلك», and «في» is attached to ركّبك, not to عدلك, for it to be as he said. The meaning of عدلك in the language is "He created you well-proportioned", one leg not longer than the other, and likewise the rest of your form. عدّلك may also be an intensive of عدلك, so they would have one meaning, as Ibn al-Zibaʿrā said: [al-ramal] 545- وعدلنا مثل بدر فاعتدل (And we made up the equivalent of Badr, so it was evened out) — i.e. we killed of them as many as they had killed of us. It was also said: عدلك means He inclined you to whatever He willed of beauty and ugliness, health and sickness.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
ما is redundant (zāʾida). Mujāhid said: [i.e.] in the likeness of a father, or a mother, or a paternal uncle, or a maternal uncle.
كَلَّا بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِالدِّينِ (9) وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ لَحافِظِينَ (10)
